title: Treasury Automation: What It Is and How to Do It
summary: What treasury automation is, the levels from a TMS to AI agents, how to automate treasury step by step, what to automate first, and the pitfalls to watch.
body_markdown:
Treasury runs on repetitive work: logging into bank portals to pull balances, rolling cash positions into spreadsheets, rebuilding the forecast every week, initiating payments, and reconciling it all at month-end. It is slow, manual, and error-prone, and it leaves the treasurer reacting to stale numbers. **Treasury automation** replaces that grind, using software to aggregate the data, run the recurring work, and surface only what needs a decision.


This guide explains what treasury automation is, the levels of automation from a TMS to AI agents, how to automate treasury step by step, what to automate first, and the pitfalls to avoid.


## **What is treasury automation?**


Treasury automation is the use of software to perform the treasury function's recurring work, cash positioning, forecasting, payments, bank reconciliation, liquidity management, and reporting, instead of doing it by hand across bank portals and spreadsheets. It spans everything from a[treasury management system](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/treasury-management-system) that automates positioning and payments by rule, to AI agents that execute the work end to end and ask the treasurer only to approve.


> Treasury automation does not remove the treasurer; it changes what the job is. Instead of assembling the cash position, the treasurer reviews it. Instead of rebuilding the forecast, they direct and approve it.


## **What treasury automation covers**


Treasury automation is not one task but a set of recurring processes, each of which can be automated to a different degree:


- **Cash positioning.** Aggregating balances across banks and entities into a single daily cash position, instead of logging into each portal.
- **Cash forecasting.** Building and refreshing the forecast from live data. See the[13-week cash flow forecast](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/13-week-cash-flow-forecast) .
- **Payments.** Initiating, approving, and tracking outbound payments with controls.
- **Bank reconciliation and cash application.** Matching bank activity to the ledger and applying incoming payments. See[cash application](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/cash-application) .
- **Liquidity management.** Positioning idle cash, managing pooling, and funding. See[liquidity management](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/liquidity-management) .
- **FX, debt, and investments.** Tracking exposures, schedules, and covenants.
- **Reporting.** Assembling board and management treasury reporting on a schedule.


## **The levels of treasury automation**


Automation is a ladder, and most teams sit in the middle. The gap at the top is where the biggest gains are:


Level What it does Human role


Manual Pull balances from bank portals into spreadsheets Does everything


Connected data Auto-aggregates bank and ERP data via a TMS or APIs Analyzes and decides


Rules-based (TMS) Automates positioning, payments, and alerts by rule Handles exceptions and judgment


Agentic Agents run forecasting, positioning, and reporting end to end Sets policy and approves


A treasury management system gets most teams to the middle: connected data and rules-based automation. The agentic level, where AI agents do the forecasting, positioning, and reporting, is the newer frontier. See[AI-native treasury](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/ai-native-treasury) for what that looks like.


## **How to automate treasury**


Automating treasury is a sequence, not a single project. A path that works:


- **1. Connect bank and ERP data.** Use[bank APIs](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/banking-apis) or a TMS to aggregate balances and transactions automatically, instead of logging into portals.
- **2. Automate cash positioning.** Produce a daily cash position across all accounts and entities without rebuilding a spreadsheet.
- **3. Automate the forecast.** Refresh the[13-week cash flow forecast](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/13-week-cash-flow-forecast) from live data rather than by hand each week.
- **4. Automate payments and reconciliation.** Run payments and bank reconciliation with approval controls and a clear audit trail.
- **5. Automate liquidity, FX, and debt tracking.** Monitor positions, exposures, and schedules continuously instead of periodically.
- **6. Automate reporting.** Assemble treasury and liquidity reporting on a schedule, traceable back to source.
- **7. Keep controls on money movement, add agents for the judgment-heavy work.** Automation does the work; people approve payments and own policy.


## **What to automate first**


Start with the foundation, then move up the stack:


- **Bank connectivity and cash positioning.** Everything else depends on having the cash data flow in automatically.
- **Cash forecasting.** The highest-leverage treasury output, and the most painful to do by hand.
- **Bank reconciliation and cash application.** High-volume matching that automation clears quickly.
- **Liquidity and treasury reporting.** Recurring reports that can be assembled on a schedule.


## **Benefits of treasury automation**


- **Real-time cash visibility.** A current cash position every day instead of a stale weekly snapshot.
- **Better forecasts.** Forecasts that refresh from live data are more accurate and far less work.
- **Time saved.** Hours of portal logins, spreadsheet updates, and manual matching disappear.
- **Stronger controls.** Automated approvals and audit trails reduce error and payment fraud risk.
- **Scales without headcount.** More accounts, entities, and volume without more treasury analysts.


## **Pitfalls to watch**


- **Payment security.** Money movement is the highest-risk area; keep strong approval controls and segregation of duties, and never fully remove the human from payments.
- **Bank connectivity and data quality.** Bank formats and connections are messy; aggregation only helps if the underlying data is clean and complete.
- **Over-automation.** Automate the work, not the judgment. Policy, funding decisions, and approvals stay with people.
- **Weak traceability.** Insist that every position, forecast, and report ties back to source so it is defensible.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is treasury automation?**


Treasury automation is the use of software to perform the treasury function's recurring work, cash positioning, forecasting, payments, bank reconciliation, liquidity management, and reporting, instead of doing it by hand across bank portals and spreadsheets. It spans rules-based automation in a TMS and AI agents that execute the work end to end.


### **How do you automate treasury?**


Connect bank and ERP data through APIs or a TMS; automate cash positioning; refresh the forecast from live data; run payments and reconciliation with controls; monitor liquidity, FX, and debt continuously; and automate reporting, while keeping approvals and policy with people. Start with bank connectivity and the cash position, since everything else depends on them.


### **What treasury processes can be automated?**


Cash positioning, cash forecasting, payments, bank reconciliation and cash application, liquidity management, FX and debt tracking, and treasury reporting can all be automated to a high degree. The judgment on funding, policy, and payment approvals stays with the treasurer, which is what keeps controls intact.


### **Do you still need a TMS to automate treasury?**


Not necessarily. A[treasury management system](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/treasury-management-system) is the traditional way to automate positioning and payments, and it works well for larger treasuries. Smaller teams increasingly automate through bank APIs and AI agents instead. See the[best treasury management software](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/best-treasury-management-software-2026) for the options.


### **What is the difference between a TMS and AI agents in treasury?**


A TMS automates treasury by rule and gives the treasurer dashboards to operate.[AI agents](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/ai-native-treasury) go further: they execute the work, building the position and forecast and assembling reporting, and ask the treasurer to approve rather than operate. One shows the cash; the other does the work.


## **The bottom line**


Treasury automation takes the manual work of aggregating balances, forecasting cash, moving money, and reporting, and hands it to software, so the treasurer directs and approves rather than assembles. The levels run from connected data and rules in a TMS to AI agents that run the work, and the gains grow the further up you go, from real-time cash visibility to treasury that scales without headcount.
